topic: Primitive growing-sieve attainment of the full-arm continuous-Napkin efficiency bound. In the iid mean-scale Verma model with W in a fixed finite alphabet with cell masses bounded below, continuous Z on [0,1], J>=3 treatment arms, bounded noisy outcomes, uniform overlap, and cellwise one-dimensional Holder smoothness s>1, target tau=c'psi with zero entries allowed. Define the regular averaged-score operator directly, with Lq=c and C=M_D+T*T, never through a fixed-z influence function. Derive the uniformly coercive full-arm optimizer q*=C^(-1)L*(LC^(-1)L*)^(-1)c, its efficiency bound, and a necessary-and-sufficient projection condition for strict gains from zero-contrast arms, including the checked three-arm odd-h witness. For B-spline dimension K_n=n^kappa with 1/(4s)<kappa<1/4, construct a cellwise cross-fitted plug-in Galerkin estimator and prove dimension-free operator perturbation, the exact training-dependent weighted-Verma remainder, global-bound asymptotic linearity, ratio-consistent variance, and uniform Wald coverage. Report a held-out Galerkin residual and active-only versus full-arm gain diagnostic; do not claim continuous/high-dimensional-W adaptation. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For fixed finite W, the plug-in multiplication-plus-finite-rank operator has a derived O_P(rho_n) operator-norm route without a K_n factor. An exact fold-conditional bias identity is second order in nuisance errors; the corrected witness yields strict gain 3 gamma^2 gamma_3^2/(sigma_3^2/3+2 gamma_3^2), and cubic-spline oracle solves converge with constraint error below 5e-16. Current checks found no collision beyond the occupied abstract geometry and fixed-basis optimization. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the uniform finite-n cellwise local-polynomial concentration lemma, including endpoint bins, denominator/clipping/fallback events and measurability, while retaining rho_n without a sieve multiplier. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the passed s=2, kappa=3/16 dimension-free operator and exact bias bounds; any unavoidable multiplier that closes the rate window should pivot or stop. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_napkin_continuous_global_efficiency.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish finite-sample, boundary-valid concentration for fold-trained cellwise local-polynomial nuisances on [0,1], including random denominators, clipping, empty-cell fallback, and measurability, that yields dimension-free operator error for the growing Napkin Galerkin system.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves boundary-adaptive pointwise and uniform concentration and Gaussian approximation for local-polynomial conditional-density estimators, but not for an operator assembled from several clipped, fold-trained Napkin nuisances.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rajita Chandak, Michael Jansson, Xinwei Ma

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies uniform approximations for locally supported splines and piecewise polynomials, including boundary cells, for ordinary regression-function inference.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Max H. Farrell, Yingjie Feng

source_refs.claim: Sharp matrix laws and local-basis arguments weaken conventional series-dimension restrictions, but their target is a regression Gram matrix rather than a nuisance-dependent multiplication-plus-finite-rank causal operator.
source_refs.author: Alexandre Belloni, Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Kengo Kato

source_refs.excerpt: no primitive learner class, rate derivation, or attainable example discharges it

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing boundary-adaptive local-polynomial and locally supported series results control functions, Gram matrices, or Studentized processes, while the Napkin application requires simultaneous fold-conditional control of several cellwise conditional means, propensities, densities, and variance functions after clipping and fallback. The prior CausalSmith review independently identifies primitive learner-side attainment as load-bearing in an analogous semiparametric construction. Here the first proof step changes to controlling all endpoint and interior denominators, numerators, failure events, and measurable learner definitions; only then can multiplication-operator geometry and fixed arm rank prevent a spurious K_n multiplier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nonasymptotic high-probability lemma covering endpoint and interior cells and all denominator, clipping, fallback, and measurability events, implying ||C_hat-C||_op=O_P(rho_n) uniformly for K_n=n^kappa without a multiplicative K_n factor.

writing_exemplar.why: Its continuous-Z discussion keeps the technical lemma tied to the motivating goal of replacing a finite-dimensional efficiency approximation by exact attainable inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Continuous-Z Napkin efficiency requires estimated nuisance functions -> a growing Galerkin inverse can amplify nuisance error -> basiswise bounds risk a fatal sieve factor -> boundary-safe dimension-free concentration is the missing bridge

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a boundary-adaptive local-polynomial estimator and prove uniform probability concentration through equivalent-kernel and empirical-process arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its endpoint treatment is the nearest published device for the [0,1] nuisance fits, although its proof must be extended to fold conditioning, clipping, fallback, and several coupled nuisances.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply noncommutative matrix concentration and local-basis/Lebesgue-factor bounds to obtain sharp growing-series Gram control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These matrix arguments can control the empirical Galerkin solve after multiplication structure removes the otherwise spurious K_n accumulation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use local support and cellwise polynomial approximation to derive uniform rates and strong approximations on compact supports.
method_exemplars.why_closest: B-splines and cellwise polynomials share the localization needed to keep endpoint and sparse-cell events from accumulating over the full sieve.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a cellwise cross-fitted growing B-spline Galerkin estimator attain the exact continuous-Z full-arm Napkin efficiency bound with a training-conditional second-order remainder, ratio-consistent variance, and uniform Wald coverage under primitive one-dimensional Holder conditions?

source_refs.claim: For continuous Z, the paper uses a finite collection of indexing functions to approximate efficient estimation rather than proving global growing-sieve attainment.
source_refs.author: Anna Guo, Lin Liu, David Benkeser, Razieh Nabi

source_refs.claim: The general Verma-efficiency paper develops finite-dimensional basis projections when exact projection is analytically intractable, without a growing-basis efficiency theorem.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: Cross-fitted regression splines yield fast, explicitly second-order remainders for average linear functionals, but the theory does not cover a nuisance-dependent inverse Verma score operator.
source_refs.author: Whitney K. Newey, James M. Robins

open_problems.why_unsolved: The fixed-basis Napkin construction avoids the central triangular-array problem. When K_n grows, the estimated influence function contains the inverse of a nuisance-dependent Galerkin operator, so cross-fitting alone does not show inverse stability, an exact training-conditional product remainder, or uniform variance consistency. Generic DML treats its orthogonal score as fixed after training, while generic spline theory controls regression error; neither directly excludes a basis-dimension factor from the multiplication-plus-finite-rank operator perturbation, and such a factor can close the root-n rate window.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified cross-fitted plug-in Galerkin estimator with dimension-free operator perturbation, an exact fold-conditional bias identity, a global asymptotic-linear expansion at the full efficient influence function, ratio-consistent variance, and uniform Wald coverage for an explicit K_n rate window.

writing_exemplar.why: Its continuous-Z section frames exact infinite-dimensional efficiency as the natural goal and finite-dimensional weighting as the presently tractable approximation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Continuous Z generates infinitely many equivalent influence functions -> exact optimal weighting is an operator problem -> the existing finite basis is only an approximation -> a growing data-driven sieve must attain the global bound

method_exemplars.technique: Use separate-sample spline fits to expose an exact second-order conditional remainder and establish semiparametric efficiency under product-rate conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The Napkin proof needs the same fold-conditional remainder calculation, but with an estimated optimal-score operator layered over the nuisance fits.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Neyman-orthogonal scores with K-fold cross-fitting to prove root-n normality and valid confidence intervals under nuisance product rates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the limit-theory template once the training-dependent Galerkin score is shown uniformly close to the population efficient score.

method_exemplars.technique: Control sieve Riesz representers and pre-asymptotic variances to prove asymptotic normality and consistent sieve-Wald variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The Galerkin optimizer is a sieve Riesz-type representer, and its estimated norm is the natural variance object for the required Wald result.

open_problems.open_problem: For continuous Z and J>=3 categorical treatment, characterize the mean-scale Napkin efficiency bound for an arbitrary linear contrast c'psi, allowing c_j=0, and determine exactly when arms absent from the contrast strictly improve efficiency.

source_refs.claim: The paper treats continuous-Z efficiency through finite-dimensional approximations and develops the main calculations treatment level by treatment level, leaving joint full-arm contrasts unresolved.
source_refs.author: Anna Guo, Lin Liu, David Benkeser, Razieh Nabi

source_refs.claim: The paper gives Hilbert-space projection and minimum-variance characterizations under mean-scale Verma restrictions but does not specialize them to joint full-arm contrasts or characterize gains from zero-contrast arms.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: The paper derives efficient estimation for general multivalued-treatment effects under ignorability, but not under a cross-arm mean-scale Verma restriction.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo

open_problems.why_unsolved: A general contrast creates a coupled vector-valued score problem: cross-arm covariance and the common Verma restriction can make an arm with c_j=0 useful as a control variate. Standard multivalued-treatment efficiency theory lacks this cross-arm restriction, while the existing Napkin calculations do not isolate the relevant projection or Schur-complement component. Consequently, the literature supplies neither a necessary-and-sufficient strict-gain criterion nor a checked nondegenerate multivalued witness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniformly coercive averaged-score operator formula for the joint optimizer and efficiency bound, an if-and-only-if projection condition for strict full-arm versus active-arm gain, and an explicit three-arm distribution realizing positive gain.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest motivation arc from a graphically identified Napkin effect to overidentification by a Verma constraint and then to efficiency gains.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Napkin effects evade standard adjustment -> the Verma restriction overidentifies each causal mean -> continuous-Z weighting creates an infinite-dimensional efficiency problem -> joint contrasts may extract information from nominally inactive arms

method_exemplars.technique: Convert the mean-scale post-fixing restriction into residualized weighted moment gradients and identify the efficient influence function by Hilbert-space projection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its closed-span orthocomplement is the exact geometric object that must be rewritten as a vector-valued averaged-score operator for the full-arm contrast.

method_exemplars.technique: Sequentially orthogonalize residuals, optimally weight the resulting moments, and prove efficiency of a sieve minimum-distance estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired full-arm solution is likewise an optimally weighted system of functional moment restrictions with an unknown operator.

open_problems.open_problem: For nested Markov models imposing several interacting Verma constraints, characterize the complete tangent-space orthocomplement and the resulting efficiency bound for a causal contrast rather than only the subspace generated by summing single-constraint directions.

source_refs.claim: The authors characterize a subspace for multiple nested Markov constraints and explicitly leave the reverse inclusion, hence completeness of the orthocomplement, open.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: The nested Markov factorization gives the graph-native collection of equality constraints induced by fixing but not semiparametric efficiency geometry for their joint imposition.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, Robin J. Evans, James M. Robins, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: The paper gives closed-form tangent-space orthocomplements for models defined by ordinary conditional independences, highlighting the missing analogue for interacting nested-Markov equality constraints.
source_refs.author: Trung Phung, Ilya Shpitser

open_problems.why_unsolved: Adding the gradient spans of individual constraints gives a valid subspace but need not exhaust their joint first-order restrictions: shared post-fixing kernels can create dependencies, intersections, and closure effects invisible constraint by constraint. Without the reverse inclusion, projection onto the summed space provides only an upper bound on the true efficiency bound and cannot certify an estimator as efficient. The obstacle is a joint completeness argument compatible with multiple fixing sequences, not another covariance calculation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality characterizing the joint orthocomplement as the closed range of an explicit block score operator, followed by the corresponding projection and efficiency-bound formula and an attaining estimator with a limit law for a named causal contrast.

writing_exemplar.why: It explicitly identifies the completeness problem and naturally escalates from solved single-constraint geometry to the unresolved joint case.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A single Verma constraint admits complete score geometry -> realistic nested Markov graphs impose several constraints -> summing individual directions proves only one inclusion -> complete joint geometry is required for a genuine efficiency bound

method_exemplars.technique: Derive closed-form orthocomplements for general conditional-independence Markov models by decomposing and recombining restriction-gradient spaces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its completeness machinery is structurally analogous but must be rebuilt for fixing-induced weighted moments instead of ordinary conditional independence.

method_exemplars.technique: Use fixing sequences, intrinsic sets, and nested factorization to obtain a complete graph-native representation of observed-law equality constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired block score operator must be indexed by these fixing-generated constraints and account for their algebraic dependencies.

method_exemplars.technique: Sequentially orthogonalize multiple functional moment restrictions and construct an optimally weighted efficient sieve estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once completeness is established, its block-orthogonalization strategy is the nearest route from the joint score operator to an attaining estimator and limit distribution.

open_problems.open_problem: Can growing tensor-product score spaces attain the efficiency bound under the full distributional Napkin Verma constraint, rather than only its mean-scale implication, when Z and the outcome are continuous?

source_refs.claim: For a single full distributional Verma constraint, the paper characterizes the orthocomplement through pairs of test functions and uses finite-dimensional basis projections when exact projection is intractable.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Anna Guo, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: The paper distinguishes invariance of the full post-fixing conditional outcome kernel from the weaker mean-scale restriction used for its causal-mean efficiency calculations.
source_refs.author: Anna Guo, Lin Liu, David Benkeser, Razieh Nabi

open_problems.why_unsolved: Mean-scale efficiency uses a one-sided function of Z, whereas the full distributional constraint generates products of treatment/Z-side and outcome-side residual test functions. The first proof step must replace the one-function averaged-score operator by a tensor-product or Hilbert-Schmidt operator and establish coercivity or regularization on a growing two-way sieve. Existing work stops at finite basis projection; generic sieve-GMM theory does not automatically handle nuisance-estimated post-fixing weights, tensor covariance degeneracy, or approximation of the complete orthocomplement.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A tensor-operator formula for the full-distribution efficient influence function and bound, with primitive conditions under which a cross-fitted growing two-way Galerkin estimator is asymptotically linear, efficient, and has a consistent variance estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Its central narrative converts full nested-Markov equality constraints into efficiency geometry and presents finite-basis projection as the tractable endpoint.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent-variable DAGs imply distributional Verma constraints -> fixing converts them to weighted orthogonality -> the complete orthocomplement yields a sharper efficiency bound -> growing tensor sieves are needed for attainable efficiency with continuous variables

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate weighted post-fixing moment restrictions indexed by two test functions and close their residualized span to characterize the orthocomplement.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the two-sided score family whose closure the tensor Galerkin construction must approximate.

method_exemplars.technique: Orthogonalize infinite-dimensional moment restrictions and use optimally weighted sieve minimum distance to attain a semiparametric bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require an estimated optimal inverse-weighting operator for functional moment restrictions containing unknown functions.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove plug-in sieve asymptotic normality and consistent variance estimation using sieve Riesz representers in conditional-moment problems.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a template for controlling tensor-sieve representers and their variances when regularity is not evident from finite-dimensional approximations.

literature_map:
Guo, Liu, Benkeser, and Nabi (2026 revision, arXiv:2512.19861) identify Napkin causal means, derive robust one-step/TMLE procedures, and obtain exact discrete-Z but finite-basis approximate continuous-Z efficiency.
Nabi, Guo, and Liu (2026, arXiv:2608.24602) convert Verma restrictions into weighted L2 orthogonality and give projection and minimum-variance efficiency characterizations.
Their mean-scale section shows how indexed weighting can exhaust a target-specific restriction, while their full-distribution section requires pairs of test functions.
The same paper uses finite-dimensional basis projections and explicitly leaves completeness under multiple Verma constraints open.
Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (2023, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1701.06686) provide the fixing and nested-factorization foundation for these equality constraints.
Phung and Shpitser (2026, arXiv:2607.23439) characterize orthocomplements for general ordinary-CI Markov models, an adjacent but non-nested setting.
Liu, Shahn, Robins, and Rotnitzky (2021, JASA, arXiv:1908.10448) show how no-direct-effect restrictions create projection-based efficiency gains in dynamic regimes.
Cattaneo (2010, Journal of Econometrics) gives efficient series estimation for multivalued treatments under ignorability but without Verma coupling across arms.
Ai and Chen (2012, Journal of Econometrics) derive efficient optimally weighted sieve minimum distance for sequential moment restrictions with unknown functions.
Chen and Pouzo (2015, Econometrica, arXiv:1411.1144) provide sieve-Riesz, Wald, QLR, and variance theory for conditional-moment models.
Newey and Robins (2018, arXiv:1801.09138) obtain exact fast cross-fit spline remainders for average linear functionals but not an estimated inverse score operator.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) supply the orthogonal-score and cross-fitting route to root-n causal inference.
Chernozhukov, Newey, and Singh (2022, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA18515) automate causal Riesz debiasing but do not address Verma-constrained operator inversion.
Belloni et al. (2015, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1212.0442) sharpen growing-series matrix laws, while Cattaneo, Farrell, and Feng (2020, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1804.04916) exploit local spline support.
Cattaneo, Chandak, Jansson, and Ma (2024, Bernoulli, arXiv:2204.10359) give boundary-adaptive uniform local-polynomial concentration; the unresolved synthesis is endpoint-safe, clipped, fold-conditional control that maps to the Napkin operator without a K_n multiplier.
